assumptions.label: Exit multiple (X), anchored
assumptions.basis: anchored: the lowest of today's multiple 36.15x, the FY2017 to FY2026 median EV/FCF 25.85x (range 15.61x to 38.47x) and 17.33x, the multiple whose implied perpetual growth at your 10% required return is 4%. Each year's EV is its last close on or before its fiscal year end times its diluted weighted-average shares on the closes' split basis, less its net cash. A past 10-K's cover count never binds, while today's multiple uses the latest one. FY2026's diluted average is 1.29% above it, so the years' multiples read high against today's.

requires.label: Required growth at the anchored exit multiple

requires.label: How often similar-sized companies delivered it
requires.basis: A frequency of reported history, not a probability. Each window is one 10-K filer's annual growth over five fiscal years in free cash flow per diluted weighted-average share, the count carried across splits through each next 10-K, grouped by starting revenue. Starts FY2003 to FY2020, from SEC's companyfacts archive of 2026-11-24 (sha256 72bc1c52670fe57a3d701f13cbab55763c122388b314d1eaca921bb18ddfbacd). Revenue's base rate is shown beside it and is never an input. Not among the 377: 38 that ended early (the filer stopped filing before year 5), 6 with no year-5 figure, 54 with no split-chained share count, 95 whose two ends use different capex or cash flow concepts and 45 that started at zero or negative free cash flow. 34 of the 377 ended at or below zero and count as -100%

figure.text: Of 377 five-year windows that began at a similar size (starting revenue USD 50.0B and up), 183 (48.5%) delivered free cash flow per share growth of at least 7.3% a year. Beside it, revenue grew at least that fast in 180 of 650 (27.7%).
